grh_e41ea2bf6e18808f3837.title: The Vagabond King
paragraphs: Poet and thief François Villon is drawn into the defense of Paris and into the orbit of King Louis and the noblewoman Katherine. His wit and courage help him rise above his criminal life for a time, but when the crisis passes he is still condemned to die for his old crimes. At the gallows Katherine invokes the king's promise and claims Villon's hand in marriage, forcing the sentence to be reversed. Villon and Katherine ride away from Paris together, with Villon promising that love will make an honest man of the Vagabond King even as the final joke leaves his old instincts intact.

grh_e4b7513964e1f9773f1b.title: Bittersweet
paragraphs: Seventy-year-old Sarah tells a younger woman how, on the eve of an arranged marriage, she ran away with poor musician Carl Linden and built a life with him across Europe. Their happiness ends in Vienna when a cavalry officer insults Sarah and Carl is fatally wounded defending her. Sarah survives by devoting herself to Carl's music, singing his songs around the world until his work becomes known. Her bittersweet story convinces the young listener to follow her own heart rather than enter a loveless marriage.

grh_e443c925d61a6ded2a6f.title: Journey Through Chaos
paragraphs: A dramatized survey of American social problems argues that the nation cannot win a war for freedom abroad while ignoring fear and division at home. Scenes examine slum housing, juvenile delinquency, racial discrimination in both North and South, and labor-management conflict. The recurring diagnosis is fear: fear of neighbors, workers, minorities and social change. The program closes by arguing that teamwork, reason and individual responsibility are needed to confront these problems rather than hiding them.

Other credited names include Anton M. Leader as director, Peter J. Harkins as radio adaptor, Clifton Fadiman as host, and Jack Costello as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.a811c0d1a6efa194|Johnson's Wax]].
This version dramatizes [[work|work.words.0eb42f617bc19f31|Journey Through Chaos]]. Agnes Meyer is credited as author and Peter J. Harkins adapted it for radio.

paragraphs: In 1918, Ellen Martin slips a note and poem into a pair of socks meant for an unknown American soldier, but the package sits forgotten until it reaches serviceman Mark Anderson decades later during another war. grh_e4bf3ea58844bc075f6c.title: Melody Ranch - When Payday Rolls Around
paragraphs: Gene opens with 'When Payday Rolls Around' and then gets caught between neighboring ranchers Buck Dean and Miss Hawkins, whose long-running feud involves survey lines, a barn, a concrete feed lot and access to water. Each has used property boundaries to get even with the other, and a dry spell makes the dispute more serious when Hawkins needs water for her ranch. Gene maneuvers the situation so Buck sees that continuing the feud will only cost both of them more. Buck finally offers her all the water she needs if she will stop trying to make him move his barn again; Hawkins accepts, the two call a truce, and the program returns to music with the quarrel finally settled.
